summary: Treosulfan (GRAFAPEX) is a bifunctional alkylating agent used in combination with fludarabine as a preparative (conditioning) regimen before allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in adults and pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with acute myeloid leukemia or myelodysplastic syndrome. It carries a boxed warning for severe and prolonged myelosuppression, which is the intended therapeutic effect; hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is required to prevent fatal complications of marrow ablation. It is a hazardous drug requiring special handling and is given as a 2-hour IV infusion on three consecutive days.
indications: In combination with fludarabine as a preparative regimen for allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in adult and pediatric patients 1 year and older with acute myeloid leukemia (AML)
In combination with fludarabine as a preparative regimen for allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in adult and pediatric patients 1 year and older with myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS)

dosage.d: 10 g/m2 body surface area per day as a 2-hour IV infusion on three consecutive days (Day -4, -3, -2)
dosage.n: Given with fludarabine 30 mg/m2/day on Days -6 to -2; stem cell infusion on Day 0

dosage.d: Premedicate with antiemetics before the first dose
dosage.n: Continue on a fixed schedule until treosulfan is completed

dosage.d: Do not exceed 10 g/m2 daily for three consecutive days
dosage.n: Higher dosages increase early morbidity and mortality

admin: Handle as a hazardous drug using applicable special handling and disposal procedures
Reconstitute prior to IV infusion per the prescribing information
Infuse over 2 hours through a secure IV line; if extravasation occurs, stop infusion immediately and manage medically
Keep skin clean and dry on infusion days, change occlusive dressings after infusion, and change diapers frequently in the 12 hours after infusion
Ensure availability of hematopoietic stem cell transplant support before administration
moa: Treosulfan is a prodrug that under physiologic conditions converts to mono- and di-epoxide alkylating species. These bifunctional alkylating intermediates cross-link DNA, producing cytotoxicity and the profound myeloablation that allows engraftment of donor hematopoietic stem cells.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to any component of the drug product
relative: Patients in whom hematopoietic stem cell transplantation cannot be ensured

preg: Treosulfan can cause fetal harm based on its mechanism of action as an alkylating agent. Advise patients of reproductive potential of the risk to a fetus and to use effective contraception during treatment. Verify pregnancy status before initiating where appropriate.
lact: Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed child, advise patients not to breastfeed during treatment and for the period specified in the prescribing information after the final dose.
renal: Specific dosing data in renal impairment are limited; administer within the transplant protocol with appropriate monitoring.
hepatic: Specific dosing data in hepatic impairment are limited; monitor liver function and manage supportively within the conditioning regimen.

major: Other myelosuppressive or cytotoxic agents - additive marrow toxicity
Live vaccines - contraindicated due to immunosuppression
moderate: Nephrotoxic or hepatotoxic agents - additive organ toxicity
Concomitant fludarabine - intended combination; manage combined toxicities
interactions.alcohol: Not applicable in the conditioning setting.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor complete blood counts, electrolytes, and organ function frequently.

serious: Severe and prolonged myelosuppression with pancytopenia
Injection site reactions and tissue necrosis with extravasation

monitoring: Complete blood counts and hematologic laboratory parameters throughout the myelosuppressive period
Signs of neurologic toxicity/seizures; consider clonazepam prophylaxis in higher-risk patients
Skin condition and infusion site for reactions/extravasation
counsel: This drug intentionally lowers your blood counts to prepare for a transplant and must be followed by a stem cell transplant
Report fever, chills, bleeding, or any sign of infection immediately
Keep skin clean and dry on infusion days as instructed
Use effective contraception and do not breastfeed during treatment
Tell the team about all medicines and avoid live vaccines
Expect nausea; antiemetics will be given on a schedule
pk: Myelosuppression develops over the days following conditioning
Plasma levels peak at the end of the 2-hour infusion
Short plasma half-life (about 1.5 to 2 hours); rapidly converts to active epoxides
Myeloablative effect persists until donor engraftment
Store per product labeling; reconstitute immediately before use
pearls: Now FDA-approved as GRAFAPEX (2025) for AML/MDS transplant conditioning with fludarabine; long used in the EU per EMA/SmPC
Boxed warning: severe and prolonged myelosuppression - stem cell transplant is mandatory to rescue the marrow
Hazardous drug: use cytotoxic handling precautions and manage extravasation as an emergency
Consider clonazepam seizure prophylaxis in higher-risk patients
Reduced-toxicity myeloablative conditioning is its therapeutic niche
missed: Treosulfan is administered as a fixed three-day inpatient conditioning schedule by the transplant team; there is no patient-managed missed dose. Any deviation in the schedule is managed by the treating team.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Overdose intensifies and prolongs myelosuppression and organ toxicity. Management is supportive with intensive hematologic support, infection prophylaxis/treatment, transfusions, and monitoring; hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is required to restore marrow function. Contact the transplant team and Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
